'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Siege of Mariupol]]
****Local officials in [[Mariupol]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], say that over 160 cars have left the city in the first successful attempt to arrange a [[humanitarian corridor]] to evacuate the city. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/over-2500-mariupol-residents-killed-so-far-war-ukrainian-presidential-advisor-2022-03-14/ (Reuters)]
***[[Russia]] denies having requested military assistance from [[China]], as alleged by several US officials. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-60732486 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/3/14/us-official-russia-seeking-military-aid-from-china (Al Jazeera)]
***A [[Russian Air Force]] [[airstrike]] on a [[television tower]] in [[Rivne Oblast]] in [[Western Ukraine]] kills at least nine people, according to Rivne governor [[Vitaliy Koval]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/nine-killed-air-strike-tv-tower-northern-ukraine-says-governor-2022-03-14/ (Reuters)]
***A Russian [[Orlan-10]] [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|UAV]] crashes near a village in [[Bistrița-Năsăud County]], [[Romania]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2022/03/14/romania-probes-drone-sighting-days-after-crash-in-croatia (Euronews)]
*[[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**[[2021–2022 Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis]]
***[[Armenia–Azerbaijan relations]]
****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Armenia)|Armenian Foreign Minister]] [[Ararat Mirzoyan]] asks the [[OSCE Minsk Group]] to help initiate [[peace talk]]s with [[Azerbaijan]] in an effort to normalize relations following the conflict. [https://theprint.in/world/armenia-asks-osce-minsk-group-to-initiate-peace-talks-with-azerbaijan/873419/?amp (''ThePrint'')]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Famine in Yemen (2016–present)|Famine in Yemen]]
***The [[United Nations]] reports that around 161,000 people in [[Yemen]] are expected to face a [[famine]] in the second half of the year. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-14/-harrowing-figures-yemen-report-says-161k-to-face-famine (Bloomberg)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 California wildfires]]
**Evacuation warnings are lifted in [[Santa Barbara County, California|Santa Barbara County]] after 50 percent of the Hollister Fire is contained. [https://www.kcra.com/article/wildfire-santa-barbara-county-described-not-typical-behavior/39421109 (KCRA-TV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
****[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on long-term care facilities]]
*****Long-term care homes in [[Ontario]] will keep their [[vaccine]] mandates for employees despite the province lifting all mandates. [https://globalnews.ca/news/8681531/ontario-long-term-care-keeping-covid-vaccine-mandates/amp/ (Global News)]
****[[Ontario]] health officials report no deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours for the first time since December 20. [https://toronto.ctvnews.ca/ontario-reports-no-new-covid-19-deaths-for-first-time-in-months-1.5818220 (CTV News Toronto)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Brunswick]]
****[[New Brunswick]] lifts their COVID-19 restrictions including their mask mandate, social distancing rules, and limits on gatherings. [https://www.cbc.ca/amp/1.6382298 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in South Korea]]
****[[Ministry of the Interior and Safety (South Korea)|Interior Minister]] [[Jeon Hae-cheol]] announces that [[South Korea]] will begin its [[COVID-19 vaccine]] campaign for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years on March 31. [[Booster dose]]s will also be administered for children between the ages of 12 and 17 years. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20220314000104 (''Korea Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
***The incidence rate for [[COVID-19]] reaches an all-time high in [[Germany]] for the third consecutive day, at a seven-day moving average rate of 1,543 infections per 100,000 people. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-14/germany-raises-alarm-as-covid-infections-surge-to-record-levels (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Mayor of Moscow|Moscow Mayor]] [[Sergey Sobyanin]] announces that [[Moscow|the city]] has ended their mask requirements and other COVID-19 measures for business. [https://www.reuters.com/world/moscow-mayor-ends-mask-requirement-citing-improving-covid-situation-2022-03-14/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
***The fourth round of talks between the [[Ukrainians|Ukrainian]] and [[Russians|Russian]] [[delegation]]s resumes in an effort to end the war but is delayed until tomorrow due to technical issues. [https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/talks-to-end-ukraine-war-resume-as-russias-offensive-grinds-on-11647255976 (''Wall Street Journal'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-negotiator-says-talks-with-russia-will-continue-tuesday-2022-03-14/ (Reuters)]
**[[Russia–Slovakia relations]]
***[[Slovakia]] expels three Russian diplomats for alleged [[espionage]] and [[bribery]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-slovakia-europe-bratislava-vienna-b3489ff284646b5439ba638264841598 (AP)]
*[[Germany–United States relations]]
**[[Germany]] announces that it will buy 35 [[Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II|F-35 Lightning II]] fighter jets from the [[United States]] to replace its aging fleet of [[Panavia Tornado]]s. Germany will also purchase 15 [[Eurofighter Typhoon]] jets from [[Airbus]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/germany-decides-principle-buy-f-35-fighter-jet-government-source-2022-03-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2022 anti-war protests in Russia]]
****[[Marina Ovsyannikova]], a [[Television in Russia|Russian state television]] journalist, interrupts a live news broadcast of [[Channel One Russia]], holding a sign saying "No War" and "Stop the war. Do not believe propaganda, they tell you lies here", and is promptly arrested. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/anti-war-protester-interrupts-live-russian-state-news-broadcast-to-denounce-invasion-of-ukraine/ar-AAV3Ppi (MSN)]
***[[Anti-war movement|Anti-war]] protesters seize the mansion of [[Oleg Deripaska]] in [[London]]. Four of the protesters who were seen on the balcony of Deripaska's mansion are later arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2022/mar/14/squatters-occupy-russian-billionaire-oleg-deripaska-london-mansion (''The Guardian'')]
**[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[Andrey Turchak]], the secretary-general of the ruling party [[United Russia]], declares that the party will draft a bill criminalising compliance with the [[Western world|Western]] sanctions. [https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/5258235 (Kommersant)]
*[[2022 Northeastern U.S. serial shooter]]
**The [[New York City Police Department]] releases images of a suspected [[serial killer]] who has shot five [[Homelessness in the United States|homeless]] men, two fatally, in [[New York City]] and [[Washington, D.C.]] in the last week. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/13/nyregion/homeless-shooting-nyc.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Cameroon]] bans [[Hookah|shisha smoking]], becoming the sixth [[Africa]]n country to do so. [https://www.africanews.com/2022/03/14/shisha-smoking-banned-in-cameroon/ (Africanews)]
